subject: Computer Networking
title: Browser Caching
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Browser Caching.

hook.text: Visit a site again and it loads faster. Your browser cached the files the first time. No re-download needed.

buildup.text: Cache-Control headers tell the browser how long to keep a file. max-age=3600 means cache for one hour.

discovery.text: ETags let the browser ask: has this file changed? The server responds 304 Not Modified if it hasn't.

twist.text: Aggressive caching causes stale content. Cache-busting adds a hash to filenames so updates are forced.

climax.text: Service workers give you full cache control in JavaScript. You can serve pages even when offline.

punchline.text: Caching speeds up the web. The trick is knowing when to let go.

quiz.question: What HTTP status code means the cached version is still valid?

details.summary: Browser caching stores copies of web resources locally to avoid re-downloading them. Cache-Control headers tell browsers how long resources stay fresh. Conditional requests check if cached resources have changed using ETags.
details.whyItMatters: Caching is the most impactful web performance optimization. A well-cached site loads in milliseconds on return visits because most resources come from the local disk instead of the network.
takeaways: Cache-Control max-age sets how long browsers keep resources fresh
ETags enable conditional requests that check for changes
Immutable file names with hashes enable aggressive long-term caching

faq.question: How does Cache-Control work?
faq.answer: Cache-Control is an HTTP header that directs caching behavior. max-age=3600 means the resource is fresh for one hour. no-cache forces revalidation before each use. no-store prevents caching entirely. public allows shared caches; private restricts to the user's browser only.

faq.question: What is cache busting?
faq.answer: Cache busting forces browsers to download a new version of a changed resource. The most common technique adds a content hash to the filename, like styles.a1b2c3.css. When the file changes, the hash changes, creating a new URL that bypasses the old cached version completely.
